cells.tense: You're building right now, and your hand is steady.
cells.verb: Building something genuinely new from what the clearing left behind
cells.place: At the center of a direction you chose and keep choosing
cells.ask: Offer to show one person the way through the part you've already worked out — walking them along the path you built — and notice that teaching it back to you keeps the practice flowing without force.
cells.core:
You're building something new on ground that got cleared for exactly this, and your hand on it is steady because you're the one holding the pen. You can feel the difference between the part that's finished and the part that's still forming, and you let each part be where it is instead of dragging it forward. Nobody has to push this. It moves because you know where it's going and go there a step at a time.
What's worth noticing is that the building doesn't need you alone. You can walk one person through what you've already worked out and it won't drain the thing — it sharpens it. The direction you chose is sturdy enough to carry someone through it with you.
cells.sheetLine: You chose this direction and you're building it, step by step, with a steady hand.

cells.tense: You're already living three months ahead of the build.
cells.verb: Cutting every corner now for a finish line nobody can see yet
cells.place: Standing over a structure that hasn't arrived, bracing for the day it does
cells.ask: Walk toward what actually connects — let one piece of shared meaning go loose in your hands and see what the people around it want it to be — and when the structure falls that needed to fall, let it belong to insight instead of to the schedule you wrote over it.
cells.core:
You're pushing the building past anywhere it's actually reached. The structure in front of you is half-formed and you're already ordering the finished version around — hauling the walls up before the foundation has settled, cutting what you'd call slack out of anyone standing near it. Every hour not spent on the build feels like it's leaking, so you add more, and the more you add the less of it is true.
The thing you're bracing for isn't coming. What's coming is the version of this that grows from the ground you're actually standing on, and you can't rush it into being by holding the schedule like a whip. Some of what you're treating as load-bearing hasn't finished being shaped yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're driving a structure that hasn't finished forming, and the driving is what's keeping it from forming.

cells.tense: There's a door you decided to walk through, and you're standing on the far side of it asking to be let back.
cells.verb: Waiting for someone to hand you a direction you already chose
cells.place: Just behind the threshold of your own decision
cells.ask: Step into the clean shape of one thing you already know how to organize — let something be clear and reliable under your hand for an hour — and when structure serves what it organizes instead of standing over it, you'll recognize your own direction arriving in the form of how things make sense in your presence.
cells.core:
You already decided. Somewhere back there the clearing happened, the way forward opened, and you stepped toward it — and then you stopped halfway, as though the decision needed a second vote you never called. You keep describing it as still being figured out. It isn't. You're the one who has to say 'this, not that,' and you've been leaving that sentence unfinished.
The shape you'd give it is right there, waiting in your hands. It doesn't need the room to agree first. It needs you to hold it clearly enough that the room can feel it.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose the direction; you're just waiting for permission that isn't coming.

cells.tense: You're building the thing and calling it the thing building itself.
cells.verb: Carrying a structure forward while insisting nobody is directing it
cells.place: Inside a direction you're already walking, denying the walk
cells.ask: Let the direction come from what you actually feel about it — one honest movement toward what genuinely engages you — and defend that one thing against the resistance, so the momentum you harvest is yours to point instead of something you pretend you're just riding.
cells.core:
You are steering this. The choices are being made, the thing is taking shape because you keep showing up and holding it to a line — and you've put the pen down in your own account of it. You'll say the project has a life of its own, the situation is what it is, the direction got set by something outside you. Meanwhile the shape it's taking is exactly the shape your hand would give it.
The momentum is real and it's gathered from your own choices. The only thing missing is you admitting the choices are yours to make, which is the same as admitting you can make them differently.
cells.sheetLine: You're already directing this build. You just haven't claimed the direction as yours.
